experiment: C8 exploratory depth-3 recursive hierarchy and error scaling
observations: Strict depth-3 recursion produced large error in all three exploratory seeds, with final/direct NMSE ratios 4.46x to 4.67x.
The strict path's large error was already present when four Level-1 recursive pair units were chained; subsequent strict recompilation largely preserved rather than repaired it.

Re-aligning each new hierarchy boundary to the corresponding original wider span before freezing and recursively compiling reduced Level-2 full-chain NMSE from about 0.22 to about 0.087 on average and Level-3 final NMSE to about 0.056.
Realign-each-level final/direct ratios were 1.11x to 1.23x and beat the single-level recursive control in all three seeds.
No held-out test data was evaluated.
interpretation: The exploratory depth-3 result suggests that recursive depth itself is not the only driver of error. Distribution mismatch at newly composed frozen boundaries dominates in the strict path, while repeated joint re-alignment at each hierarchy boundary can repair much of that mismatch before the next recursive compile. Fresh confirmatory testing is required.
